- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for short-term (1–3 day) forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment reversal 1–2 days ahead.
- For long-term (10+ day) forecasts, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply smoothing or decay factor (e.g., 0.85) to reduce momentum bias.
